messages.author: 0f051a4b7efa96c4
messages.subject: qplot and commandArgs problem
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to write a simple .R script to produce plots from a .csv file specified in the command line.

for example, the following will plot LSS vs RSS from the scott_dose.csv file:

scott.smith@cougar:/home/scott.smith {31} Rscript Rtest.R scott_dose.csv LSS RSS

and the .R script is:

library(ggplot2)
args <- commandArgs(TRUE)

data<-data.frame(read.csv(args[1]))
attach(data)

x <- args[1]
y <- args[2]
z <- args[3]

x
y
z


qplot(y,z)

ggsave("~/tmp/RTest.png")

browseURL("~/tmp/RTest.png")

which produces a graph output, but with no data plotted:

scott.smith@cougar:/home/scott.smith {31} Rscript Rtest.R scott_dose.csv LSS RSS
Loading required package: methods
[1] "scott_dose.csv"
[1] "LSS"
[1] "RSS"
Saving 7 x 7 in image

Basically my "y" and "z" variables from commandArgs aren't being picked up by qplot. I'm sure it is something very simple, but I'm a relative beginner to R.

thanks, Scott

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: qplot and commandArgs problem
parts:
Probably change your script to

p <- qplot( y, z )
ggsave("~/tmp/RTest.png", plot=p)

qplot doesn't produce any output inside of a script without being
explicitly print'ed.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: qplot and commandArgs problem
parts:
I wouldn't say that's empty. There is clearly at least one point located at z,y, which makes me think that it's an issue with ""'s. 

I think it is plotting text versus text instead of your values. I believe you need to use ggplot(data=data, aes_string(x=y, y=z))+geom_point()
